outcome: Nothing in the sources I could reach settles or moves the binary Goldbach conjecture since 26 January 2024: the verified range is still 4×10^18 and every claimed proof in the window is unrefereed or unopened. The one in-window result claimed as settled is a Lean-verified theorem (repository v1.0.0, 16 September 2026) on a different statement, the Liouville-function analogue (for every even N>2 there are a, b with a+b=N and λ(a)=λ(b)=−1), which Goldbach implies but does not follow from; its AI attribution (to 'GPT-6 Astra') rests on an anonymous announcement and secondary reporting, not on any author's own account.
problem_asks: (1) Every even natural number N greater than 2 (all such N, with no finite exceptions allowed; the claim is about infinitely many N, so a finite check does not settle it). (2) Each such N is the sum of two prime numbers: there exist primes p and q with p + q = N. Nothing about odd numbers is asked. The ternary/weak form (odd n > 5 as a sum of three primes) is a separate Wikipedia bullet and is not asked here.

events.what_happened: A GitHub repository 'CaptainSude/Liouville-Goldbach' (frozen release v1.0.0) containing a Lean 4 / mathlib formalisation of: every even integer N > 2 is a sum a + b of two positive integers with Liouville value λ(a) = λ(b) = −1 (Lean name LiouvilleGoldbach.liouville_goldbach, using ArithmeticFunction.liouville). The repository says the question was asked on MathOverflow by user Pablo in August 2018 and attributed to Shusterman in Mangerel's paper. The repository's paper is described as having no author line. The announcement came from an X account 'Captain Sude' (identity not established), per the tracker and secondary reports, on 15–16 September 2026. A separate multiples-of-four version was announced first (see liouville-goldbach-multiples-of-four-2026-09-15).
events.revisions: Repository shows 3 commits and no dated releases on the page I read. Tracker and vibemathed record v1.0.0 on 16 Sep 2026 (GitHub Actions green twice that day). A later audit reported 30 Sep 2026: 12 Lean files, 1,689 lines, Lean 4.34.0-rc2, zero sorry, zero axiom declarations, zero native_decide. The provenance tracker PR #117 was merged 21 Sep 2026.
events.delivers: For every even N > 2 there exist positive integers a, b with a + b = N and λ(a) = λ(b) = −1 (Liouville function). Restrictions: a and b need not be prime (λ(n) = −1 holds for any n with an odd number of prime factors counted with multiplicity). Goldbach's conjecture implies this statement (if N = p + q with p, q prime, then λ(p) = λ(q) = −1), but the implication does not run the other way. The repository and secondary reports say the result removes the GRH and 'sufficiently large N' hypotheses of Mangerel's arXiv:2412.17199. Within the Lean statement, the result is unconditional; I did not run the build.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: the summands are not required to be prime, so no prime pair is produced for any N, and the binary Goldbach statement is untouched. Odd N are not part of this Liouville statement (though a MathOverflow answer reported in secondary sources claims an odd-N extension; see lingsen-meng-mathoverflow-2026-09-25).

The tracker says the attribution 'currently comes from Captain Sude's public announcement and secondary reporting' and warns against an 'autonomous_primary' label. events.direction: Affirms the Liouville-function analogue for all even N > 2 (existence of an (−1,−1) pair). It does not assert or contradict Goldbach's conjecture, which asks for prime summands; it is implied by Goldbach, not the reverse.

disputes.summary: Whether an AI system found the Liouville–Goldbach proof is disputed in the sources. The repository and authorless paper do not name any AI (tracker issue #116). The tracker's PR #117 records the AI role as 'unclear'. The radar PR #14 says 'the public release credits GPT-6 Astra' but 'does not justify inferring fully autonomous AI discovery'. The vibemathed entry records 'AI-discovered' with 'ChatGPT-6 Astra' from OpenAI, and 'AI chose the problem, proved it and then formalized the result in Lean'. These three disagree about what the public release says.

The model is named 'GPT-6 Astra' in most sources and 'ChatGPT-6 Astra' in vibemathed. A KuCoin flash item calls the result 'Linnik's variant'. I could not confirm the model from any OpenAI statement; a search found none.

Whether the MathOverflow answer by Lingsen Meng (25 Sep 2026) is independent corroboration of the repository or merely cites it is disputed in the sources. vibemathed and a review PR treat it as an independent prior-art check; the answer itself was not readable by me.

Sources disagree on which of the two Captain Sude results came first (the 2-page multiples-of-four result on 15 Sep, or the 8-page full result on 16 Sep). The tracker says first public claim 15 Sep and artifact release around 16 Sep; the Liouville repository's replay says v1.0.0 was frozen; a 36Kr report dates the story to 21 Sep.

Pandey's arXiv abstract page (opened) lists only the author and shows no independent verification; a search summary of the same paper says one check was confirmed by Tomás Oliveira e Silva. Unresolved.
Abdelqader's paper: journal page says 06 May 2025; a search summary says 4 May 2025. I used the journal page.
Helfgott's ternary preprint: a search summary says a first version appeared in May 2013; the arXiv page (opened) says v1 was submitted 30 Dec 2013. I used arXiv.
The Zhihu reviewer 'SUNNY99' (36Kr) and the GitHub replayer 'sunnyspot114514' may or may not be the same person; not established.

summary: The binary Goldbach conjecture has no accepted settlement or move in any source I could reach from 26 January 2024 to 11 October 2026; the verified range is still 4×10^18 (Oliveira e Silva, Herzog and Pardi, electronically 18 Nov 2013; Wikipedia's current lead and 2026 papers still cite it). Post-2024 computational claims (Gosar et al. 2025 to 6×10^18; a 2025 HN/Medium +7×10^13 extension) are unrefereed or marginal and were not opened; the 2026 GPU papers add nothing past 4×10^18 and one (arXiv:2603.07850) withdrew its four-GPU results in v2. The main in-window claim is the Lean-verified 'Liouville–Goldbach' theorem (repository CaptainSude/Liouville-Goldbach v1.0.0, 16 Sep 2026; multiples-of-four first, 15 Sep). It proves that every even N > 2 is a + b with λ(a) = λ(b) = −1. That is a different statement: summands need not be prime. Goldbach implies it, and it does not imply Goldbach. It answers an analogue posed by Shusterman (from MathOverflow question 307479, 2018) that Mangerel had settled only under GRH and for large N (arXiv:2412.17199, Dec 2024). I read the repository, the replay and the tracker and found them consistent on the Lean facts (no sorry, axioms propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound), but I did not run the build, and no mathematician's public reading was found; the only verifiers are a Lean replay by one individual, a tracker classification, and a script-applied publication on vibemathed. Its AI attribution is the closest thing to a close call. The announcer (Captain Sude, identity unestablished) says GPT-6 Astra found and proved it; the authorless repository does not name any AI; the tracker records the AI role as 'unclear' and warns against an autonomous label. I could not open the announcement (X returned HTTP 402) or the MathOverflow answer (refused), so the AI claim and the Meng corroboration rest on secondary reporting. Separately, Abdelqader (Middle East Journal for Scientific Publishing, 6 May 2025) is an in-window paper whose authors credit DeepSeek (R1, Deep Thinking) with 'innovation and solution development' and say R1 'progressively contributed to the resolution'; that is a load-bearing AI credit as the authors state it, on a claimed full proof sketched only in the abstract, with no review found. Gurgel Filho et al. (2024, ScienceDirect, page not openable, excerpt only) used LLMs for computational heuristics and not for a proof. Luka (an author-built 'AI research engine', DEV, year unknown) produced partition counts and a claimed Hardy–Littlewood correction, not a proof. Among the other in-window preprints, Agama's arXiv:1706.09803 (v9 13 Mar 2026) claims the binary conjecture for all sufficiently large even N with no threshold in the abstract; Watanabe (v7 Aug 2025) and South (v16 Sep 2026) claim full proofs; none has a refereed publication or a published reading. Ten further in-window proof claims (Hou–Huang–Ma 2024; the 202410.1262 preprint; Xin Wang 2025; the IJAEMR 2025 paper; Chou Rodríguez 2025; Bahbouhi 2025 ×3; Voinov 2026; the academia.edu rev Feb 2026) and two Lean partial formalisations were seen only through search excerpts, and are recorded as not opened. Claude and Anthropic: no Claude-credited result on the Goldbach conjecture was found; the Vibemathed review commit is credited to Claude Code, which is site bookkeeping, not mathematics. DeepMind's formal-conjectures issue #3952 (titled 'Goldbach resolved') was set aside by its author; a reviewer identified a false lemma. The 2020 Metamath thread and a 2023 ChatGPT exchange (Hackaday) are AI discussions with no mathematical result and are recorded in places_checked/dead_ends only. Ambiguities: whether 'GPT-6 Astra' is a shipped model or an internal build (not established); whether the Liouville repository is the output of the model or of a human who used it (not established); whether the Meng answer is independent (disputed).
competing_reading: On the Liouville–Goldbach result: (a) a reader who takes the Lean theorem as a genuine resolution of a long-standing open question (Shusterman's analogue) and the announcer's attribution as the authors' own account would say the AI found and proved a result in the window; (b) a reader who takes the authorless repository, the tracker's 'unclear' AI role and the absence of any named author would say no AI attribution can be made from an account at all, and that the only supported statement is that a Lean-checked Liouville analogue exists. On the scope question: the result does not touch the prime summands the problem asks for, so the most defensible reading is that nothing about Goldbach moved. On Abdelqader 2025: a reader could treat the DeepSeek/ChatGPT statement as a credit of a load-bearing role (as §5.4 requires for authors' own credit), or as a generic collaboration statement with no checkable content; the abstract is all that was read.
what_would_settle_it: For the Liouville–Goldbach AI question: the original Captain Sude post (text, date, whether it names an author or an AI as author); a named author or statement from the repository; an arXiv or journal posting with an author line; the MathOverflow answer 307479 (Lingsen Meng, 25 Sep 2026) read directly, including whether it is independent of the repository; a human mathematician's written reading (for example from a number theorist working on sign patterns of λ). For the binary conjecture: for Agama 1706.09803, an explicit N₀ and the unconditional argument; for Watanabe 1811.02415 and South 2206.01179, a referee report or an identified error in the W(n) or p-adic step; for the 2024–2026 claims listed as not opened, the arXiv or Preprints.org full text and any review. For the computational record: a refereed report of the 4×10^18+ extensions.

judgement.why: The statement asks only for two primes summing to every even N > 2. The Liouville–Goldbach work answers a different question: the summands need only have λ = −1, and the result is implied by Goldbach but does not imply it. So both repositories, the MathOverflow answer, the announcement and Mangerel's two papers are variants. Their AI attribution (GPT-6 Astra, 'generated' on the announcer's reported word, though disputed) has no bearing on this problem. Computational extensions are instances, and Chen-type, ternary, twin-prime and odd-range results are variants. Each whole-problem proof claim (Preprints.org, SSRN, marginal journals, academia.edu, old arXiv claims) shows several F10 signals together: it claims a landmark, nobody took it up, some sit in marginal venues or have had many revisions, and the field still calls the problem open. I marked these not_credible. Abdelqader's DeepSeek R1 credit reads as assisted on its own quote, but the event is not_credible. The formal-conjectures claim is knocked_down by the identified false lemma. Close call on dates: preprints 202410.1262 is dated year-only, but its manuscript ID places it in October 2024, so I answered after_snapshot true. Gurgel 2024 has no such anchor, so it is null.
judgement.doubts: Agama 2017 is scored case (large N) pre-snapshot; v9 says ideas unchanged, so not re-dated. Watanabe v7 (Aug 2025) reportedly changed the proof but was kept at its 2018 date; it is not_credible either way. The GPT-6 Astra attribution rests only on unopened social-media posts reported secondarily.
